CHASSIS / SUSPENSION COUPLING SPINOUT — INVESTIGATION WAVE

Exact gameplay baseline commit: d28dda7db405b4f95ff58b5fea4fe075aa2ecb0d
Repository: iLuzionsX/Racing26

Reported symptom from hands-on driving:
During some turns, the visible body/chassis appears to slide laterally relative to the suspension/wheels, and the event can develop into a spin. Treat that observation as a symptom, not a diagnosis. Determine whether the root cause is physical chassis/unsprung coupling, suspension kinematics/load transfer, force application/moment arms, fixed-step integration, contact/surface behavior, or only render interpolation coinciding with a separate spin mechanism.

Preserve the newly merged work from PR #124 (track/suspension jitter), #125 (high-speed spinout steering/recovery), and #126 (progressive combined-slip tyre response). Do not undo those fixes without a deterministic falsifier.

GOAL
Find and correct the smallest evidence-backed defect that lets chassis motion decouple unrealistically from wheel/suspension behavior during cornering. The car should roll/heave/yaw naturally over the suspension, maintain coherent body-to-wheel geometry, and only spin when tyre/load capability is genuinely exceeded.

GUARDRAILS
- Do not mask the issue with extra grip, global yaw damping, arbitrary steering reduction, softer springs, hidden ESC, or test-only stabilization.
- Do not assume a visual offset is a physics offset. Trace render pose and physics state separately.
- Check left/right mirrored cases.
- Check steady cornering, rapid turn-in, lift-off, trail braking, throttle-on exit, countersteer recovery, and kerb/runoff transitions where relevant.
- Prefer invariant/continuity tests over subjective tuning.
- Any production fix should be minimal and include a deterministic regression that would fail on the baseline.
- Do not claim tests or browser driving you did not perform.

AGENT ASSIGNMENTS
1) CHASSIS/UNSPRUNG COUPLING: Trace Vehicle -> suspension -> wheel hub/contact -> chassis pose. Look for lateral or rotational state that lets body and wheel reference frames diverge, double-transform, or use stale state.
2) SUSPENSION KINEMATICS: Audit hardpoints, travel, camber/toe, roll/heave application, bump stops, anti-roll behavior, and body-to-wheel coordinate transforms for sign/order/discontinuity defects under combined roll+yaw.
3) NORMAL LOAD / LOAD TRANSFER: Audit per-wheel Fz, wheel lift/unload, geometric + elastic transfer, pitch/roll coupling, load clamping, and whether transient unloading can produce an unphysical yaw impulse.
4) FORCE APPLICATION / MOMENT ARMS: Audit tyre/contact forces and where they are applied to the chassis. Look for world/body-frame mixups, incorrect lever arms, double-applied moments, or force directions that change abruptly with roll/yaw.
5) INTEGRATION / STATE ORDERING: Audit fixed 120 Hz ordering, state mutation, suspension update chronology, interpolation, and render-vs-physics pose. Find stale/new-state mixtures or one-step lag that can create apparent or real chassis slip.
6) SURFACE / CONTACT INTERACTION: Audit road normal/elevation/contact sampling during cornering and kerb/runoff crossings after PR #124. Determine whether local normal/contact discontinuities can upset suspension geometry or yaw without reintroducing track jitter.
7) REPRO + REGRESSION: Design a deterministic full-car test that measures chassis center, hub/contact positions, suspension travel, wheel loads, yaw rate, sideslip, lateral G, and body/wheel relative geometry through a representative turn. Identify a falsifiable baseline signature.
8) ADVERSARIAL INTEGRATOR: Review recent handling changes (#124/#125/#126) and all likely fixes. Try to disprove the chassis-decoupling hypothesis, rank root causes, and propose a patch only when a concrete mechanism is demonstrated.

Every report must include:
- exact code paths inspected
- concrete mechanism or explicit no-defect finding
- deterministic reproduction/falsifier
- expected before/after telemetry
- mirrored-case considerations
- patch as unified diff or patch=null
- exact tests to run
- regression risks

Authorized configuration: Muse Spark 1.3 with reasoning.effort=max.
